newsitem.title: IRAN: Tajik government, opposition open talks in Iran.
newsitem.headline: Tajik government, opposition open talks in Iran.

text.p: Tajikistan government officials and opposition leaders opened talks on Monday in Tehran on power sharing in the turbulent central Asian country.

Tajik Foreign Minister Talbak Nazarov, the head of the Islamic opposition delegation Akbar Turajonzada and United Nations special envoy Gerd Merrem were attending the talks which were expected to last two weeks, Iranian media said.

The meeting would cover details of an accord signed in Moscow last month by the two sides to try to halt four years of bloody conflict. The deal called for an immediate ceasefire, an amnesty, an exchange of war prisoners and the creation of a Commission of National Reconciliation.
The composition of the commission was expected to be one of the main issues under discussion, U.N. sources have said.

Iranian press reports earlier said the opposition had proposed that the government and the opposition each get a 40 percent representation on the commission, with the remaining 20 percent going to unspecified "other forces". The government had rejected the plan, the reports added.

After years of broken ceasefires, Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri last month signed the agreement, saying that their country of nearly six million people had suffered enough.
Tens of thousands of people have been killed in a four-year civil war between Tajikistan's secular government and Islamist guerrillas, spawned by the collapse of the Soviet Union.
A 96-member U.N. Mission of Observers in Tajikistan (UNMOT) works with a much larger peacekeeping force fielded by Russia and the Commonwealth of Independent States.
The rebels control the mountainous eastern half of Tajikistan, which houses about 10 percent of the population.
